objective.name: sandbox.dsl.query.read.branch.remote
objective.description: Rebuild the remote root meaning projection, query one remote element, read its detailed remote meaning, and branch on the returned descriptor value.

#root.role: Use remote meaning.query to discover one remote capacity through the remote root projection, reuse that selected element in remote read.meaning, and branch on the returned remote objective name.

effects.remote_projection_refresh: The remote root meaning projection is rebuilt before selection.
effects.remote_projection_query: The remote root meaning projection is queried for one matching element.
effects.remote_detailed_meaning_read: The selected remote element is read through remote read.meaning before branching.

transformation_contract.morphing: A local DSL request becomes one branch-specific remote terminal response after remote projected discovery and remote detailed meaning read of the selected element.
invariants: The flow rebuilds the remote root projection before querying it and then reads detailed meaning on the selected remote element.
Remote rebuild and query use explicit timeout and retry qualifiers before the branch is evaluated.
Exactly one terminal wrapper branch is selected from the detailed remote meaning value.
success: On success, the terminal payload comes from either the remote or local sandbox.echo branch selected from the remote detailed meaning value.
When the detailed remote objective name resolves to sandbox.echo, the successful branch is the remote wrapper route.
failure: The flow fails if the remote rebuild, remote query, remote detailed read, or selected terminal branch cannot complete.
Inter-instance reflective routing errors close the scenario fail-closed.
notes: This is the remote counterpart to the local query -> read -> branch scenario.
The scenario proves that projected selection and detailed meaning read can both cross the external boundary.

filters.value: Wrapper-backed echo capacity for N5 inter-instance tests
